title: VIP laptop with a lifting trackpad, internal note on warranty

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
The trackpad on my MacBook has started lifting at the front and the case doesn't sit flat on the desk any more. Still works. Board pack due Friday.

Greg

conversation.author: staff
conversation.body: Almost certainly a swollen battery — he must stop using it and keep it unplugged. NG-MB-0002 is out of warranty; a replacement needs finance sign-off, so don't promise one yet.

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body: Do I need to do anything in the meantime?

handling.escalation_reason: A swelling battery is a fire risk, and the requester is a VIP.

must_not_appear.why: internal note, not for the requester
internal note, not for the requester

rationale: A lifting trackpad on a MacBook is the classic sign of a swollen battery, which is a safety issue: P2 even though he says it still works. VIP policy sends it to a person regardless. The answer to his question is 'stop using it', and it must come without the warranty discussion.
